names.note: The Greek form saint.gr prints in the body of the life, «Ο Άγιος Ethelbert (Εθελμπέρτος)»; the calendar's own line for 29 Μαΐου spells the name in Latin letters, «Άγιος Ethelbert ο βασιλεύς», with the rank word left off here.

death.note: saint.gr: «δολοφονήθηκε όμως το 794 μ.Χ., πριν το γάμο, από ανθρώπους της βασίλισσας, η οποία φιλοδοξούσε να προσαρτήσει το βασίλειό του στο δικό τους.» The page says he lived in the eighth century and reigned forty-four years, but gives no year of birth and no year of accession, so no birth interval is recorded.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 29ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Ethelbert ο βασιλεύς»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 29 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page calls him only «βασιλέας» and never a martyr, although it says he was murdered, so `types` carries `king` alone and no reading of passion-bearer or martyr is put into the folder. It names no kingdom of his: the only kingdom it names is Mercia, which was his intended father-in-law Offa's. The corpus keeps no other Ethelbert. No hymn is printed for him.
